extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and legal researchers (practitioners and students of patent law)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal rules governing patents licenses, licensor/licencee rights and duties, scope and construction of licenses, remedies (fees, rescission, injunction), implied licenses (vendee/employer), transfers, and limitations (time/place/quantity). Focused on doctrinal criteria used to evaluate or draft patent licenses and related disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensor must be owner to grant valid license
rubrics_metrics.description: A license is invalid unless the licensor is an owner of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the licensor had assigned all his interest, grant may be invalid. Federal courts may decide whether a license exists; license granted by one co-owner may have particular effects (see co-owner entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses carry no greater rights than licensor possessed
rubrics_metrics.description: A license carries no rights exceeding those of the licensor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license cannot grant rights that the licensor did not own or could not convey; subject to all prior conveyances and the licensor's remaining power to assign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive vs. non-exclusive licenses — form and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses may be exclusive or non-exclusive; exclusive licenses have particular protections and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive licenses (form and effect discussed) may be protected against third parties by injunction; an exclusive license usually coupled with license to make; exclusive status affects remedies and estoppel issues. Exclusive licenses may be invaded by licensor and such conflicts are treated specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses may be express or implied; written or oral
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may be express (written or oral) or implied from circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express written licenses merge prior parol agreements and bar parol evidence to vary them; oral licenses may be valid (e.g., to sell as agent). Implied licenses arise in many contexts (vendee, employer, estoppel) and have specific conditions for recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and scope of license measured by claims and patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of a license is measured by and construed with reference to the patent and the Claim to which it is limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope may also be ascertained by the instrument itself, the conduct of the parties, and by construing several instruments together; moral conditions outside the instrument do not determine scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express restrictions in license are binding and violation is infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Express restrictions (time, place, manner, purpose, quantity, specified shop or business) in a license bind the licensee; violation of such express restrictions is infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include license limited to use in a certain shop, for a certain number, or for certain purposes. A license that grants use only under stated conditions warrants use only under those conditions; breaches can be sued as infringement or for breach of contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses can be limited as to time, place, or quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may validly be restricted as to time, place, or quantity, and such restrictions define the licensed rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations like 'in a certain shop' or 'to a certain extent' can prohibit other uses; if not restricted in terms, license generally gives broad rights during the patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to make/use/sell are distinct rights but may imply others
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may transfer the right to make, to use, or to sell; the typical license to sell is usually coupled with a license to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license to make may carry right to sell; a license to use may carry the right to make if necessary to enjoy the license; licenses do not extend beyond what is necessary for enjoyment unless expressly granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: License under foreign patent does not authorize sale in United States
rubrics_metrics.description: A license under a foreign patent does not authorize sale of the patented subject in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-border effect depends on the territorial scope of patents; licenses are generally effective only in the territory of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses may be granted before issue and under expired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may be granted before the issue of the patent and a license under an expired patent is not fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses granted before patent issue are construed by the patent as granted; licenses may run during a patent extension only if so expressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express covenants on validity and estoppel of licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees who accept licenses (especially with covenants not to contest validity) may be estopped from denying patent validity while enjoying the benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covenant not to deny validity is enforceable; licensee stamping articles with patent mark cannot deny validity as to those articles; estoppel may not apply after licensor repudiates or after license expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty and consideration rules (royalties as consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Royalties are the consideration for a license; failure to pay royalties is not, by itself, infringement though equity may rescind the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee liable for royalties while enjoying the license; licensee sued for overdue fees may defend on failure of consideration, want of title, judgment of invalidity, or eviction; licensee cannot set up other licensees paying lower rates as defense to owe fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocability and irrevocability of licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses may be revocable for cause unless they are unconditional for the term or paid for by a gross sum in advance (irrevocable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unconditional license for the patent term or paid up in gross is irrevocable; otherwise revocable for cause. Forfeiture provisions must be stipulated to operate; rescission in equity generally required rather than mere notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture, rescission, and abandonment of licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A license may be forfeited or rescinded for breach or specified causes, but rescission usually requires equitable proceedings rather than mere notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not forfeited for mere non-payment unless stipulated; surrender by one co-licensee does not bind others; licensor seeking rescission may be denied equitable aid if he has broken his contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability — licenses generally personal and not transferable
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses are generally personal and not transferable unless intent to transfer appears or instrument allows transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses 'to use' or 'in his own business' are normally non-transferable; license to 'and his assigns' is not always transferable; gross-sum-paid licenses and certain sales-related licenses may be transferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied license to purchaser (exhaustion doctrine for article sold)
rubrics_metrics.description: A lawful, unconditional sale of a patented article by patentee (or authorized party) implies a license in favor of the purchaser to use the article; that license covers the article sold and other parts necessary to its use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendee's license continues until the article is used up; purchaser may repair the article but not rebuild or replace it; implied license arises only from lawful and unconditional sale and rests on common law principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied license in employer-employee context
rubrics_metrics.description: An implied license in favor of an employer may arise where employee inventions are concerned, giving the employer the right to practice the art during the patent life or use the article until used up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when employer-employee relationships, including corporation/public or private corporation contexts, or where employee receives express license; conditions vary by facts and jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee bound by contract even if not read
rubrics_metrics.description: A license binds the licensee even though he did not read it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee must fulfill his contract or is liable for breach and may be treated as an infringer; failure to read the instrument is not a defense to contractual obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation by licensee may be sued either on contract or for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee who violates the license may be sued either for breach of contract or for patent infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations are provided; choice of remedy may affect available relief (contract damages vs. injunction/damages for infringement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensor's duties regarding enforcement against infringers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the licensor covenants to prosecute infringers, he fulfills the agreement if he stops them in any way; licensor is not necessarily bound to protect licensee against claims under adverse patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensor's covenant to sue does not prevent licensee from suing in the licensor's name; licensor not estopped to deny validity when sued by licensee for failing to prosecute; details depend on covenant wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel and acquiescence can create licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel or acquiescence in use may operate to create an implied license or prevent the patentee from asserting rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances implying a license must be evaluated; mere judgment without satisfaction ordinarily does not estop; long unlawful use does not imply license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording/license recording not required but gives notice effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Record of license is not required, but recording produces constructive notice effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net constructive notice principles apply; failure to record does not invalidate license but affects notice to subsequent purchasers or assignees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair vs. rebuild — rights of licensee/vendee
rubrics_metrics.description: A license or the vendee's implied license carries the right to repair the article while its identity remains, but not to rebuild or replace by a new article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repair is allowed to maintain the article; reconstruction or replacement that destroys identity may be infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses linked to patent term and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A license typically expires with the original term of the patent unless extension or other expression provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License to use a specific article may authorize use until the article is used up even if patent extended; license may run during a patent extension only if so expressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to multiple rights and limitations as to specific article numbers or parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A license covering a certain number of articles carries the right to keep that number complete; licenses limited to particular articles do not authorize other articles unless necessary for enjoyment of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an article is covered by several patents, a license may avail as to all; license under one patent or claim gives no protection against another patent unless encompassed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee remedies against licensor for breach or fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee has remedies against licensor for breach of contract, fraud, refusal to supply articles, refusal to reduce royalties as agreed, or for wrongfully licensing others; remedies include rescission, specific performance, and damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may recover money paid for fraud or mistake, may sue for royalties when patent declared invalid under certain circumstances, and may seek equitable relief depending on facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee's liability for royalties on sales and accounting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee may be liable for royalties on sales even after assignment or on articles sold after license terminated depending on breach; accounting presumptions may apply if licensee refuses to show accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee sued for royalties on sales is presumed to have sold as much as at last accounting if he refuses to produce accounts; limitations and defenses include showing superior title or eviction.
